budgeting-scheduling: How accurate is a development budget?

Can you budget from a treatment?
Yes, as an early estimate range. A detailed budget needs a script.
Is the budget used once production starts?
Yes. It becomes the baseline that Line Production manages against.
Can you re-budget an existing budget?
Yes. We review it against the script and production realities, and show you where it holds and where it doesn’t.

Yes. We review what you have, find the story in it, and plan what’s still needed.
How long does a documentary take?

feature-films: Do I have to use Kemsor for every stage?
No. Pick the stage you need. Many features use us for one stage only.
Do I need a star attached to get financed?
It can help, but it isn’t the only thing financiers look at. A strong script, an honest package and a budget that holds up often matter as much.
Can a feature be made well on a modest budget?
Yes, if it’s planned for that budget from the start. We show scenario budgets and what each one changes on screen.
Can you step in when a feature has stalled?
Yes. We look at where it’s stuck, what’s already in place, and re-plan from there.
festival-awards: Can you get my film into a festival?
No one honestly can. We give the film its best chance: the right targets, strong materials, and on-time submissions.
Should a short film do festivals?
Often, yes. Festivals are one of the main ways short films find audiences and recognition. We’ll help you choose the right ones.
My film has already screened. Is it too late?
Not necessarily. Many festivals accept regional or other premiere status. We check each one.
How much does a festival run cost?
It depends on the number of festivals, fees, and travel. We plan a festival budget with you before submissions begin.

What do I need before we talk?
A script or a strong treatment is enough to start. We help build the rest: the creative package, budget, schedule and production plan.
Can investors approach Kemsor looking for projects?

post-production: What is post-production in film?
Post-production is everything that happens after the shoot: editing, sound, colour grading, VFX, music and delivery. It’s the stage where footage becomes a finished film.
What does a post-production supervisor do?

A post-production supervisor plans and runs the whole post pipeline. That means the schedule, the budget, the teams, the review rounds and the final deliverables, so every department stays in sync until the master is delivered.
I already have an editor. Do I need post-production supervision?
Your editor shapes the cut. Supervision keeps the sound, colour, VFX, music and delivery teams working to the same schedule and budget around that cut. The two roles work best together.
When should post-production supervision start?
Ideally before the shoot, so workflow, data handling and delivery requirements are planned from day one. Most projects come to us after wrap, and that works well too.
Can you finish a film shot by another company?
Yes. We regularly take over projects that were shot elsewhere, check the footage and records, and plan the post-production workflow from there.
Is it too late if we’re already deep in post?
No. We can take over a stalled film edit, re-plan the schedule and budget, and get the film delivered.
What happens if we need changes after picture lock?
Changes are possible, but each one can affect sound, VFX, colour and music. We show you the time and cost before anything is committed, so you can decide with full information.
What deliverables do OTT platforms require?

Usually a picture master, a final mix and stems, subtitles and captions, delivery paperwork and a QC report. The exact list comes from each platform’s own spec, such as Netflix or Amazon Prime delivery specs, and we build to that.
Which formats do you finish?
Feature films, web series and OTT projects, documentaries and short films.
Do you edit, mix and grade in-house?
We supervise the full post pipeline and bring in the right editorial, sound, colour and VFX teams for each project.
